Ps2.title: 7 C’s of Effective Communication
Ps2.summary: The 7 C's of communication provide principles and guidelines to effectively communicate so that targeted groups understand the intended purpose and influence others.

sections.heading: 7 C’s OF EFFECTIVE COMMUNICATION
paragraphs: The 7 C’s of communication are the principles explained to:
Effectively communicate so that the targeted group may understand the intended purpose.
Offer guidelines for individuals to learn how effectively they can influence people with their own or organizational agendas.
list: 1. COMPLETENESS – It refers to a communication between sender and receiver when all the relevant information has been sent by the sender after analyzing the receiver’s mindset by ensuring no necessary information is missed during communication.

1. COMPLETENESS (Clarification) – In case the intellectual level of the receiver demands clarification concerning the information provided; the sender should be in a position to satisfy the receiver by answering the relevant queries. This will result in effective communication with completeness of information. Otherwise, the communication will not be effective.
2. CONCISENESS – During interaction, the use of accurate information in short sentences will be considered as a concise way of communication.
2. CONCISENESS (Outcome) – Provisioning of concise useful information would be much regarded as effective communication while the response from the audience will also be positive.
2. CONCISENESS (Keyword) – To the point.
3. CONSIDERATION – It refers to a communication where the advantage of the receiver is given due attention by respecting the mental perception and awareness of the receiver.
3. CONSIDERATION (Focus) – The communication mainly focuses on the needs, thoughts and requirements of the receivers with a positive approach.

3. CONSIDERATION (Example) – The interaction of political leaders with the public is mainly describing the needs and problems of the people, which are directly influencing the targeted group of people and play an emotional part in it.
3. CONSIDERATION (Keyword) – About people.
4. CONCRETENESS – Concreteness refers to the specifics where interaction is performed with preciseness or by referring to statistics.
4. CONCRETENESS (Effect) – This creates a pronounced effect on the receivers as compared to the general talks.
5. CLARITY – The endeavor for effective communication is to transfer your thoughts and ideas into the mind of the receiver.
5. CLARITY (Execution) – It can effectively occur when a simple, precise and easy set of words are used for communication in order to express the purpose without going into extensive interaction.
5. CLARITY (Keyword) – Simplicity.
6. COURTESY – A polite word can play a prominent role in resolving disputes among people.
6. COURTESY (Importance) – Understanding the mentality of receivers of information and their feelings towards the intended interaction is very important for effective communication.
6. COURTESY (Effect) – It creates a long lasting effect even if there is a difference of opinion between communicating with people or organizations.
6. COURTESY (Keyword) – Respect for Audience.
7. CORRECTNESS – It refers to the factual accuracy of words used in communication between or people communicating with organizations.
7. CORRECTNESS (Application) – It is important in both verbal and non-verbal communication where selection of correct words at the right time is important.
7. CORRECTNESS (Keyword) – Facts or Proofread.
